**Answer**

No existing administrative region satisfies all seven of the listed criteria.

**Why the conditions cannot coexist**

| Criterion | What it demands | Incompatibility |
|-----------|-----------------|-----------------|
| 1. Area 3 500–5 000 km² | The region’s land area must fall within this range. | – |
| 2. Current name adopted 1860–1875 | The name change must have occurred during this period. | – |
| 3. Region established 1816–1822 | The administrative unit must have been created in those years. | – |
| 4. Name derived from a canal | The region’s current name must literally reference a canal. | – |
| 5. Canal excavated 1630–1670 | The canal used for the naming must have been dug in this window. | – |
| 6. Current name 6–10 years after canal excavation | If the canal was dug 1630–1670, the name must have been adopted 6–10 years later, i.e. 1636–1680. | **Conflict** – this window (1636–1680) does not overlap with 1860–1875 required by criterion 2. |
| 7. About 30–35 colleges | The region must host roughly that many higher‑education institutions. | – |

Because criteria 5 and 6 force the name‑adoption period to be 1636‑1680, while criterion 2 requires it to be 1860‑1875, there is no overlap between the two timeframes. Therefore no single real‑world region can meet all requirements simultaneously. The impossibility is intrinsic to the stated constraints, not a matter of missing data.
